module_title: MS PowerPoint - Advanced Interface Views and Master Slides
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical IT exams, this module analyzes the different 'Views' used to organize a presentation and the powerful 'Slide Master' tool used for global formatting.

core_concepts.title: Normal View
core_concepts.description: The default editing view in PowerPoint. It displays a large central area for editing the current slide, and a left-side pane showing small thumbnails of all slides in the presentation.

core_concepts.title: Slide Sorter View
core_concepts.description: A view that displays all slides in the presentation simultaneously as miniature thumbnails arranged in horizontal rows. It is strictly used to easily reorganize, reorder, delete, or duplicate multiple slides at once.

core_concepts.title: Slide Master
core_concepts.description: Found under the 'View' tab, this is a powerful global template tool. If you want to place a company logo on all 50 slides, or change the title font for the entire presentation, you do it ONCE in the Slide Master. The change automatically cascades to every slide.

core_concepts.title: Reading View
core_concepts.description: Similar to Slide Show view, but it does not take over the entire screen. It plays the presentation within a resizable window with the Windows taskbar still visible, allowing you to multitask.

important_entities.name: Notes Page (Speaker Notes)
important_entities.significance: A dedicated text pane below the slide where the presenter can type speaking prompts or scripts. During a presentation, these notes are visible only on the presenter's laptop screen, NOT on the projector screen shown to the audience.

important_entities.name: Handout Master
important_entities.significance: Controls the layout of printed copies of the presentation given to the audience. You can configure it to print 2, 3, 4, 6, or 9 slides per physical sheet of A4 paper.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common Tier-2 statement-based trap asks: 'Can you edit the text inside a slide while in Slide Sorter view?' The answer is NO. Slide Sorter is purely for managing the order and sequence of slides. To edit text, you must return to Normal View.
Aspirants sometimes assume 'Slide Show' is the default mode. Always remember that PowerPoint defaults strictly to 'Normal View' upon opening.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Think of the Slide Master as the absolute boss. Whatever formatting rule the Master dictates, every other slide automatically obeys.

exam_strategy_tips: In Mains papers, expect questions on the exact function of the 'Slide Sorter'. Whenever you see keywords like 'rearrange', 'reorder', or 'view all thumbnails', the answer is unequivocally Slide Sorter View.
